about: Single source of truth for body radii used by the moons viewer and, later, the atlas. radius_km is the value to draw and to take altitudes against. label_radius_km is only the unit in which the PDS moon-centred trajectory files express distance; it converts those files to km and is never used as a surface.

sources.atlas_table: Galileo Data Atlas body table (values chosen by the owner as the working set)
sources.iau2015: Archinal et al. (2018), Report of the IAU Working Group on Cartographic Coordinates and Rotational Elements: 2015, Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astr. 130:22, as listed by JPL SSD Planetary Satellite Physical Parameters (ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sats/phys_par)
sources.pds_label: GO_POS_SC_MOONCRDS_DS.TXT Table 1 and the *CRDS.LBL files: distances expressed in satellite radii (RI = 1818, RE = 1560, RG = 2634, RC = 2409, Amalthea R = 86.2 km)
sources.nssdca: NSSDCA Jovian Satellite Fact Sheet, Radius (km) column
sources.orbtrtrj: GP_0001/DATA/DWE/ORBTRTRJ.TAB bodies table (REQ, RPOL); PROBETRJ.LBL JOVIAN 1-BAR RADIUS

IO.name: Io
IO.note: atlas table is 0.11 km above the IAU 2015 mean radius, inside its 0.50 km uncertainty

AMALTHEA.name: Amalthea
AMALTHEA.note: radius_km is the mean radius; the body is drawn as the triaxial figure
